a: Token bucket allows bursts up to capacity while refilling tokens at a steady rate.
Leaky bucket smooths traffic to a constant outflow rate.
Fixed window counts requests per interval; simple but can burst at boundaries.
Sliding window log stores timestamps for precise limiting at higher memory cost.
Sliding window counter approximates sliding behavior with less memory.
Use Redis or similar so limits are shared across all app instances.
Rate limits control short-term speed; quotas control longer-term total usage.
HTTP 429 signals the client should slow down; include Retry-After when possible.
Limit by API key, IP, user id, or a combination depending on abuse mode.
Return clear JSON errors and remaining quota headers for good DX.
